description: I am a biomedical engineering student leading a multidisciplinary project to develop an interactive space game that blends biology, life support, and space exploration. Our goal is to leverage real NASA open-source data to create an engaging simulation centered on health, physiology, or ecosystems in space. We are looking for teammates with skills in programming, UI/UX design, or 2D/3D art who are excited to collaborate and bring this vision to life!
summary: ORBIT: THE LAST OUTPOST is an interactive educational space-survival game developed to make learning about space exploration more engaging and practical. Players control a spaceship, hit targets, and answer STEM questions about five essential systems: Energy, Radiation, Nutrition, Safety, and Astronomy. Correct answers earn points and help maintain the outpost, while incorrect answers and environmental hazards threaten its survival. As players progress, challenges become more difficult, testing their scientific knowledge and decision-making skills. At the end of each mission, a personalized report displays scores, accuracy, strengths, weaknesses, and learning recommendations. ORBIT addresses NASA's challenge by turning complex space-engineering concepts into an accessible, interactive experience. It is important because it encourages scientific curiosity, critical thinking, and problem-solving while helping young learners understand the decisions involved in sustaining human life beyond Earth.
details:
ORBIT: THE LAST OUTPOST is an interactive educational space-survival game designed to make learning about space exploration more engaging and accessible. Players control a spaceship, navigate through space, and interact with targets that trigger scientific questions. These questions cover five essential areas: Energy, Radiation, Nutrition, Safety, and Astronomy. Correct answers earn points and support the mission, while incorrect answers and environmental hazards make survival more difficult. At the end of the game, players receive a personalized report showing their performance, strengths, weaknesses, and areas for improvement.

The project aims to help students understand the scientific challenges of sustaining human life beyond Earth. It encourages scientific curiosity, critical thinking, problem-solving, and informed decision-making by turning complex concepts into an interactive experience.

We developed the game using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with HTML Canvas for game graphics and interactions, and local storage for saving progress where applicable. We also used NASA's open scientific resources as references to make the questions and survival scenarios more realistic.

The creative aspect of ORBIT is the way it connects knowledge with consequences: players do not simply answer questions; their understanding of science becomes part of their survival strategy. Our team considered educational value, scientific accuracy, gameplay simplicity, accessibility, user engagement, and the gradual increase in difficulty.

Ultimately, ORBIT aims to inspire the next generation of explorers by showing that scientific knowledge is essential to humanity's future in space.
